symptoms.description_en: Pain, pressure, tightness, or squeezing in the center or left of the chest.
Sensation of rapid, strong, fluttering, or irregular heartbeats.
Swelling of one or both legs, ankles, or feet due to fluid retention.
Brief loss of consciousness due to inadequate blood flow to the brain.
Difficulty breathing, feeling winded, or tight chest causing breathlessness.
Sudden, noisy expulsion of air from the lungs, dry or producing phlegm.
Hemoptysis — blood or blood-streaked mucus coughed up from the lungs.
High-pitched whistling sound when breathing, especially when exhaling.
Pain or aching in the head or upper neck region.
Sensation of spinning, unsteadiness, or lightheadedness.
Sudden uncontrolled electrical disturbance in the brain causing shaking or loss of consciousness.
Loss of sensation or pins-and-needles feeling in limbs or face.
Sudden changes in awareness, orientation, or thinking ability.
Pain or discomfort felt anywhere in the stomach or belly region.
Feeling of sickness in the stomach with or without actual vomiting.
Loose, watery stools occurring more than three times in a day.
Presence of blood in feces — bright red, dark, or black tarry stools.
Yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes due to high bilirubin.
Body temperature elevated above normal (typically 38°C / 100.4°F or higher).
Extreme tiredness, weariness, or lack of energy that does not improve with rest.
Significant unintentional weight loss (more than 5% of body weight in 6 months).
Repeated episodes of excessive sweating during sleep.
Pain, stiffness, or discomfort located in the upper, middle, or lower back.
Pain, swelling, or stiffness in any joint — knee, hip, shoulder, wrist, or ankle.
Sudden or progressive loss of muscle strength, especially in limbs.
Intense worry, fear, or physical symptoms like racing heart and shortness of breath.
Persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in daily activities.
Thoughts of harming or killing oneself.
Pain, scratchiness, or irritation in the throat, often worsened by swallowing.
Pain or discomfort inside or around the ear.
Partial or complete inability to hear in one or both ears.
Burning, stinging, or discomfort when urinating.
Presence of blood in urine (hematuria), making it pink, red, or brown.
Change in skin appearance — redness, itching, swelling, or blisters.
Life-threatening allergic reaction with swelling, hives, breathing difficulty, and low blood pressure.
Abnormally increased thirst even after drinking adequate amounts of fluid.
Needing to urinate more often than usual, including at night.
Uncontrolled active bleeding that does not stop with direct pressure.
Sudden face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty — possible stroke.
Tissue damage caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, or radiation.
Unexpected or heavy vaginal bleeding outside of normal menstrual period.
Fever in a child under 12, especially critical in infants under 3 months.

triage_rules.rule_name: Chest Pain with Associated Cardiac Red Flags

recommendations.content_en: Call emergency services (112 or local equivalent) immediately. Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
Sit down, rest, and try to remain calm. Chew a standard aspirin tablet if you are not allergic.
Seek immediate emergency care. Sit upright and loosen tight clothing.
Rest, drink plenty of fluids, and monitor your temperature.
